o1.biggest_strength: It leads with the in-app checkout fix and prices it correctly at about 558 orders and ₹34 lakh a month. Every run time and smallest effect is worked out from real session counts, and they check out (9.9%, 6.3%, 5.5%).
o1.biggest_mistake: It has no test aimed at the firmness question. Firmness is only touched through review filter tabs. The calendar dates and the two-lane overlap add complexity I did not ask for.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a plain-words firmness test. Show the funnel-by-browser maths in one simple table. Drop the invented calendar dates or tie them to real launch constraints.

o2.biggest_strength: The diagnostic table splits the funnel by device and browser, and every rate in it is right. It ties the 4,130 in-app errors to the 4,800 lost carts. It adds an A/A test and event tracking before testing starts, and it covers firmness, which is the second-biggest chat topic.
o2.biggest_mistake: Test 5 bundles the new hero image with the moved reviews. If it wins, I won't know which change worked.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Split test 5 into two tests or justify the bundle. Give the profit value of each test's smallest effect, not only the one general 10% example.

reason: Both get the checkout bug, the money and the sample-size maths right. Output 2 is easier to read, sets up clean tracking with an A/A check, and tests firmness, so it's the plan I'd hand my team, though Output 1's per-test maths is a bit sharper.
